doc.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025

title: Mistakes in improvisation
summary: White says mistakes can become part of the movement because every note is a half-step from something good.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Are there mistakes that you can make? Because the reason I ask that is of the middle generation of musicians I’ve asked about mistakes in improvisation most of them say there’s no mistakes.

You know its funny you should say that. I feel – I felt mistakes all the time, but if you’re going to create you’re going to make mistakes. But the good part, and what I think they refer to is if you can make something happen from those mistakes. You know? Which you can do. I mean really every note is just a half-step away from something that’s good so you just make it part of the movement. But you know I started, this is something that people don’t know, but I play traditional New Orleans jazz mainly but I also go all the way to the other end and play a little avant garde.
